# Fridgeweek

> A free printable weekly planner for family life: one week, seven equal days,
> filled in by hand and stuck on the fridge. No app, no account, no sync.

Fridgeweek turns a handful of parameters into a print-ready sheet. It is built
for households with pre-school and early-school children: every day gets the
same height so a child who cannot read yet finds today by counting rows, and
every writing line opens with a strip of marks — one per person, plus a house
for the whole household — so circling a mark says whose line it is.

The sheet is generated in the browser and printed. Nothing is stored on a
server, there are no accounts, and the configuration lives in the page's own
address so a link is the sheet. It is MIT licensed and prints in 15 languages,
on A4 or Letter.

## Pages

- [Home](https://fridgeweek.com/): what the sheet is, how a family uses it, and samples.
- [Make a sheet](https://fridgeweek.com/sheet): the builder — set people, marks, lines per day, header, paper and language, then print or download a PDF.
- [About](https://fridgeweek.com/about): what it is, privacy, terms, licences and credits.

## Project

- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/eckberg/fridgeweek): the whole project, MIT licensed.
- [DESIGN.md](https://github.com/eckberg/fridgeweek/blob/main/DESIGN.md): every product decision and the reason for it, including what Fridgeweek deliberately will not do.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/eckberg/fridgeweek/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): how to add a language or a symbol.
